sara: paging — spike in KV cache entries + continuous-batching amplification. Alert: kvcache.size increased 4x in 5m, p95 gen latency up to 3.2s, some timeouts. Notifying oncall. :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created (sev=S2). Pager: alex. Alert payload: kvcache.size=520k, growth_rate=+420k/5m, batch.replay_count=1800/min.

alex: I'm on. any quick mitigations? can we toggle speculative decoding or roll back batch config?

sara: logs indicate speculative decoding agents are writing duplicate KV entries when draft/target reorder happens during continuous batching — causes replays and cache blowup. Example from serving node 14:```
[2026-03-15T02:12:03Z] spec-decode: draft_id=abc123 target_seq=45 request_id=req-7f1 write_kv(key=ctx:xyz, size=1.2k)
[2026-03-15T02:12:03Z] batch-replay: request_id=req-7f1 duplicate_write detected, replay_count=3
[2026-03-15T02:12:04Z] kvcache: size=512341 entries=512341
```

molly: AcmeCorp reported ~25% failures on generation endpoints ~02:10-02:20 UTC. They're on Dedicated pool A. Marking customer-impact.

kai: quick mitigation path: disable speculative decoding globally via runtime flag while we patch. Command I can run: `rbctl set-flag --cluster=prod --flag=spec-decode false` — low risk and reversible. Also consider capping max batch tokens: `max_batch_tokens=1024` to reduce reordering.

alex: +1 to disabling spec-decode. I'll also push a batch cap override to pool A: `rbctl update-pool --pool=dedicated-A --override='{"max_batch_tokens":1024}'`

sara: starting canary deploy of both mitigations to canary nodes (serving-canary-1, serving-canary-2). Will monitor `kvcache.size`, `batch.replay_count`, and `spec.decode_violations`.

ops-bot: Deploy initiated by sara: patch/1823456791; canary: 2/2; command: `deploy --patch patch/1823456791 --env=prod --canary=2` ETA ~90s. Rollout link: https://console.internal/deploy/patch/1823456791

tessa: note — disabling spec-decode will increase p50 by ~40ms on small seqs but should cut p99 dramatically. OK from product side for short mitigation. :thumbsup:

alex: canary metrics: canaries show kvcache growth halted, `kvcache.size` stabilized at ~130k, p95 down to 760ms from 3.2s. Applying rollout to remaining nodes in pool A.

molly: customer update: AcmeCorp confirms failures dropped to ~1.2% and latency improved. They're seeing timeouts vanish.

raj: quick root-cause hypothesis: speculative-decoding write path doesn't respect the batch reorder canonical sequence; when continuous-batching reorders draft->target resolution, we end up writing multiple KV entries for same logical position and dedupe logic misses due to missing ordering marker. Amplifies with large batch sizes and high concurrency.

sara: mitigation success. Next steps: open follow-up ticket to add ordering metadata to KV writes and strengthen dedupe to include (request_id, draft_seq, model_epoch). Also add an integration test that simulates worst-case reorder + high-concurrency batching.

alex: created ticket INF-2371: `kvcache: add ordering markers + dedupe by request/seq`, linked to CI load test. Assigning to eng-runtime.

sara: oncall handoff at 10:30 UTC to raj. Leaving runbook notes: monitor metrics `kvcache.size`, `batch.replay_count`, `spec.decode_violations`, and `grpc-generate-p95`.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. Next oncall: raj. Incident severity downgraded to S3; monitoring mode.

ops-bot: Patch rolled out to pool A: success. patch/1823456791 completed at 1823456882, rollouts: 16/16 nodes. No rollback triggered.

raj: will run a targeted load test (batch-alignment worst-case) at 11:00 UTC to validate permanent fix. Also will schedule a brief postmortem doc and customer-facing summary.

sara: thanks all — closing paging loop. If any regressions re-appear, re-open INC-2026-042 and ping #eng-oncall. :white_check_mark:
